A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same register-neuron research, with matching authors, methods, and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including identification of relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuron interventions, classification and dense-prediction experiments, object discovery, VLM evaluations, and typographic-attack results.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds attention-bias experiments, InternViT-6B evaluation, and additional controls and analyses.

M1.justification: The original register-discovery and activation-shifting method remains. However, Section 6.2 and Appendix A.2 introduce a distinct alternative: zero register-neuron activations and inject constant attention key/value biases estimated from test-time registers, eliminating the additional token. Algorithm 2 documents the existing shifting procedure rather than introducing another method change.

E1.justification: The datasets and task requirements are retained, including classification, segmentation, depth estimation, object discovery, eight VLM benchmarks, and RTA-100 attacks. InternViT-6B is tested on the existing VOC/COCO tasks. The typographic-attack experiment moves to Appendix A.8 rather than disappearing.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark comparators remain unchanged. v5 adds random-neuron editing to the typographic-attack comparison (Table 12), selected-versus-random neuron zeroing in Section 6.2, and uncompensated register-neuron zeroing in the attention-bias comparison (Table 7). Random-neuron controls already existed for outlier relocation in v1, but these comparison contexts are new.

E3.justification: v5 adds evaluation using InternViT-6B, a zeroing-and-bias-recovery experimental design, and NYUd linear probing with zero through five registers. Previously, register-count evaluation examined value-update similarity and attention maps. Reported dense-prediction metric coverage also narrows: v1's auxiliary mAcc, aAcc, AbsRel, and delta accuracy metrics are omitted. These changes do not establish revisions to the retained benchmark splits or training budgets.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether register-neuron zeroing damages accuracy and attention biases recover it, whether random edits suppress typographic attacks, and whether additional registers improve depth estimation. Appendices A.10–A.11 add earlier-layer activation maps and comparisons of residual-update magnitude and directional consistency. Existing initialization, relocation, decoder-weight, and LOST analyses largely remain.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without reported repeated-run uncertainty. v5 Appendix A.13 specifies three independent seeds and 95% confidence intervals for the main linear probes. Random-neuron controls also report three trials or random sets with variation, and the register-count depth table includes uncertainty. This establishes newly reported statistical practice, not that v1 necessarily used fewer runs.

E6.justification: v5 adds attention-bias, InternViT-6B, register-count depth, and residual-update results. Its new InternViT comparison reports VOC2012 corloc of 35.4 without intervention and 48.7 with a register (Table 11). Existing Table 2 summaries change slightly, including DINOv2 ImageNet accuracy from 86.3 to 86.4 and ADE20k mIoU from 48.2 to 48.3; auxiliary dense-prediction results are removed. The new zeroing baseline is inconsistent: 70.4% in Section 6.2 versus 71.3% in Table 7.

T1.justification: v5 introduces an analytical model, Proposition 1 connecting register neurons to attention sinks and no-op attention, and Corollary 1 concerning attention-bias equivalence, with derivations in Appendix A.1. These use normalization-free, identity-projection attention and null-space assumptions. v1's attention-output decomposition is retained as Equation 19; it did not contain these propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central training-free-register claim remains, but v5's abstract and contribution summary add a mathematical account, and its introduction claims artifact suppression through attention biases without additional tokens. VLM interpretability language is narrowed to cleaner attention-based text-to-image attribution. Typographic defense loses its introductory emphasis but remains an evaluated application.

C2.justification: v5 develops v1's brief attention-bias interpretation into a no-op/null-space explanation and connects sink removal to accuracy loss. It strengthens the interpretation of typographic experiments to argue that local information is lost from computation rather than redistributed, linking this to dense prediction. It also discusses possible language-model applications and positional-encoding contributions while retaining the principal limitations.

D1.justification: v5 adds explicit shifting pseudocode, guidance for selecting the outlier threshold and neuron count, and technical settings for the additions, including averaging register keys/values over 1000 images and selecting 300 InternViT neurons. The original method's principal settings and project/code access information remain. Much of Algorithm 2 formalizes previously described operations.

R1.justification: Beyond the largely retained related-work survey, v5 substantially expands positioning around no-op attention, attention biases, and language-model outliers, citing Clark, Kobayashi, Bondarenko, Gu, and quantization research. It also distinguishes its intervention from Nakamura et al.'s inference-time attention engineering. Publication and URL updates for retained references are bibliographic changes rather than new positioning.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: typographic attacks move from the main experiments to the appendix, a mathematical-model section enters the main text, and the detailed OpenCLIP activation-distribution discussion moves into reorganized supplementary analyses. New algorithm-overview and hyperparameter sections accompany revisions to the abstract, contribution framing, and terminology.

P2.justification: v5 adds algorithm diagrams, attention-bias plots and visualizations, an InternViT visualization, a residual-update figure, and new result tables. Existing displays are also reorganized: Tables 4–5 become side by side, Algorithm 1 becomes compact, and the two auxiliary dense-prediction tables are replaced by a combined confidence-interval table. Relocated attention maps and attack figures remain identifiable.

improvement.justification: Additional controls, attention-bias experiments, InternViT-6B validation, and three-seed confidence intervals strengthen the empirical support, while clearer intervention and parameter-selection instructions improve reproducibility. These benefits are qualified by lost auxiliary metrics and weaknesses in the new material: Proposition 1 omits the positive query–sink alignment needed by its proof, and the zeroing baseline is inconsistent between Section 6.2 and Table 7. The net improvement is supported chiefly by stronger empirical validation, with limited credit warranted for the new formal guarantees.
